items.title: Fast and slow inputs have different controlled river responses

source.label: River signal timescale experiment

metricDefinitions.label: Controlled SD ratio
metricDefinitions.definition: The receiver-equal mean outlet standard deviation divided by that of the same instantaneous source mixture; input correlation time is relative to each network's mean nominal travel time.

caveats: Input covariance and common-memory strength are imposed scenarios, not measured DOC timescales or lake residence times.
The common unit-gain kernel allocates part of the shared-corridor travel budget to spreading while preserving every path mean.
The 32 networks contain 89 source paths and seven overlapping-catchment systems; paths are not independent field replicates.

preview.note: Four declared endpoint scenarios from the complete saved timescale/coherence/memory grid.

items.title: The same paths can separate or align constructed upstream waves

source.label: Loch Vale pathway illustration
filters: Two fixed actual Loch Vale gauge-to-receiver paths
Identical unit-amplitude source waves and period
Synchronous or constructed 3π/4 source phase advance

metricDefinitions.label: Amplitude ratio
metricDefinitions.definition: Constructed outlet wave amplitude divided by the amplitude of the same instantaneous upstream mixture, with source weights and individual path means held fixed.

caveats: Only the mapped path lengths are observed; the input wave phases are constructed and do not explain the measured Loch Vale signal by themselves.
A ratio above one can result from removing input cancellation. It is not increased source concentration, carbon production or DOC removal.
The shared-corridor kernel is conservative and imposed; no physical speed or residence time is estimated.

preview.note: Four transport cases; the two aligned-arrival reference rows remain in the complete scenario file.

items.title: The same-input working point does not establish a fixed whole-form ranking

source.label: Controlled broad–elongated comparison
filters: Four elongated and eight broad networks
Five complete catchment systems resampled 5,000 times

metricDefinitions.label: Form difference
metricDefinitions.definition: The arithmetic receiver-mean controlled SD ratio in broad networks minus that in elongated networks at the fixed working point.

caveats: The interval spans zero for both real-edge route definitions.
The controlled arithmetic difference is a different estimand and forcing population from the previous observed geometric-mean SD contrast.
No kernel strength or source phase is selected to fit the observed whole-form contrast.

preview.note: The fixed working-point form contrast from each independently retained routing definition.
